parts.text: In this experiment you will determine the focal length of a converging lens. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 3.1. Fig. 3.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Arrange the apparatus as shown in Fig. 3.1. Place the lens a distance u = 20.0 cm from the illuminated triangle. Place the screen near the lens. Move the screen until a sharp image of the triangle is seen on the screen.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Measure the distance v between the lens and the screen as indicated in Fig. 3.1. v = .................................................... [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate a value f 1 for the focal length of the lens. Use the equation f 1 = uv ( u + v ) . f 1 = .................................................... [1] Method 2

ms.label: 3(a)(ii)
ms.text: correct calculation of f1 with unit

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Keep the screen in the same position so that the values of u and v are the same as in (a).

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Move the lens closer to the screen until another sharp image of the triangle is seen on the screen. Fig. 3.2 Measure the new distance u between the illuminated triangle and the lens as indicated in Fig. 3.2. u = .......................................................... Measure the new distance v between the lens and the screen. v = .......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 3(b)(i)
ms.text:
u within ± 10% of v from (a)(i)
v between 18 cm and 22 cm

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate a second value f 2 for the focal length of the lens. Use the equation f 2 = uv ( u + v ) . f 2 = .................................................... [1] Method 3

ms.label: 3(b)(ii)
ms.text: f2 and f1 to consistent 2 or consistent 3 significant figures

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Keep the screen in the same position so that the values of u and v are the same as in (b).

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Measure h O , the height of the illuminated triangle, as indicated in Fig. 3.2. h O = .......................................................... Measure h I , the height of the image of the triangle on the screen. h I = .......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 3(c)(i)
ms.text: sensible value for hO and hI < 1.0 (cm)

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate a value M for the magnification, using the equation M = h I h O . M = .................................................... [1]

ms.label: 3(c)(ii)
ms.text: correct calculation of M and no unit

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate a third value f 3 for the focal length of the lens. Use your value of v from (b)(i) and the equation f 3 = v ( M + 1) . f 3 = .................................................... [1]

ms.label: 3(c)(iii)
ms.text: f3 in range 12.0 cm to 18.0 cm

ms.label: 3(d)
ms.text:
any one from:
mark position of lens on holder
clamp rule / place rule on bench
ensure screen, lens and object all perpendicular
view scale perpendicularly

ms.label: 3(e)(i)
ms.text: difficult to measure height of image (accurately) as image is small

ms.label: 3(e)(ii)
ms.text: use larger object / graph paper on screen OR mark top and bottom of image and measure later
